messages:
maria (PM): FYI — Sales just escalated a parity ask from two mid-market customers: they want per-customer model pinning + region-aware routing. They said competitor has it and it's blocking purchase. Need quick triage.
anna (Eng Lead): What exactly do they mean by pinning? persistent binding of a customer to a model binary/version across requests? or per-request hinting?
zach (SE): Quote from ACME: "We need to guarantee the model version used for our enterprise data, and route to EU-only infra — otherwise we can't certify compliance." They called it a "pin".
priya (CS): Same ask from FinServ co. Both care about auditability + predictable outputs. Also asked for rollout controls (canary + instant rollback).
devon (PMM): This is a positioning issue too — if we can't match this pattern customers will default to the other vendor for large deals. Can we scope an MVP that we can market as "per-customer model controls"?
anna (Eng Lead): Engineering constraints: full per-customer binary isolation is heavy (storage + ops). We can do a policy-based pin where customer config picks from a small set of model variants already loaded on nodes. That gives strong guarantees for version stability but not full binary isolation. Latency/cost implications minimal if we reuse warmed KV caches.
maria (PM): OK propose we define 2-track scope: MVP = policy pinning to model variants + region routing + audit log for model selection. V2 = per-customer dedicated model binaries (heavy).
zach (SE): MVP sounds acceptable to customers if we commit to rollout timeline and clear limits. They care about an SLA for model-version consistency and an audit trail.
anna (Eng Lead): Rough ETA for MVP: 6 sprints (includes routing policy, config API, audit logs, console controls). Can accelerate to 4 sprints if we cut canary automation (manual canary).
devon (PMM): What are the launch acceptance criteria? Need something concrete for sales.
maria (PM): Draft acceptance criteria: 1) Customer can pin to a named model variant in Console/API and the system uses that variant for all their requests. 2) Region routing honors customer policy (EU/US) with fallback rules. 3) Audit logs capture model variant selection per request for 30 days. 4) No P95 latency regression >20% on typical gen workloads. 5) Pilot with 3 customers and rollout plan + rollback.
priya (CS): Add: runbook for CS to enable/disable pinning per-customer and checklist for compliance request response time.
anna (Eng Lead): One implementation note: prefix caching semantics mean pinning to a heavily-quantized variant might change output quality. We should include a quality-check step in pilot — compare 100 sample prompts across variants.
maria (PM): Good call. Add automated evals as requirement for pilot.
zach (SE): Customers asked about pricing — they expect an incremental surcharge for pinned capacity. We should define a pricing guardrail.
devon (PMM): Suggest "pin surcharge" as % of usage or reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated. We can draft later but sales needs a placeholder.
anna (Eng Lead): Risk list: 1) Operational complexity for upgrades/revocations, 2) output regressions when switching variants, 3) storage cost if we go per-customer binaries.
maria (PM): Decision needed: Approve MVP scope and timeline (6 sprints with manual canary) or push to V2. If approved we'll schedule an RFC and engineering spike to firm estimates.
devon (PMM): Recommend approve MVP. We need something to cite in deals.
priya (CS): +1 from CS. We can recruit 2 pilot customers.
zach (SE): +1 from Sales, will start soft-commit with ACME once we have acceptance criteria and rough timeline.
anna (Eng Lead): +1 conditional on spike to validate cache/warmup assumptions (1 sprint).
maria (PM): Okay I'll book spike and RFC. Spike owner: @anna. If spike confirms, we lock scope and commit to 6-sprint delivery with manual canary.
prod-bot: RFC created: rfc/2026-04-per-customer-pinning-draft (link) :white_check_mark:
maria (PM): Thanks team — I'll send an update to Sales + Ops with the acceptance criteria and pilot asks. We'll reassess after spike results.
